title: History 10: From frames to space-time: the road to modern video models

questions.q: A Wan run has a causal VAE. Does that mean the denoiser can't see later frames?
options: No. Causal is about the VAE, and the sampler updates every latent frame at every step
Yes. Each frame is sampled before the next
Yes, unless you raise the steps
No, because the VAE isn't used
questions.answer: No. Causal is about the VAE, and the sampler updates every latent frame at every step
questions.why: A frame-by-frame model is a different design, covered in CU-503.

questions.q: You ask for 48 frames from a 4k + 1 family. What comes back?
options: 45, because 48 floors to 12 latent frames and 12 decodes to 45
questions.answer: 45, because 48 floors to 12 latent frames and 12 decodes to 45
questions.why: The empty-latent node floors, and 4 L − 3 is the way back. The lab prints this row.

questions.q: In the lab, what does changing frames 6 to 8 do to outputs 0 to 5 under causal padding?
options: They change by the same amount as under centred padding
questions.why: Output t reads only t − 2, t − 1 and t.

questions.q: Why does factorising space and time save more on a longer clip?
options: Joint pairs grow with the square of all tokens, while spatial pairs grow in line with the frames
The VAE compresses long clips more
questions.answer: Joint pairs grow with the square of all tokens, while spatial pairs grow in line with the frames
questions.why: 20.7 times at 81 frames and 40.0 times at 161, in the lab.

questions.q: What is the price of factorised attention?
options: Something at another place and another time takes two layers to arrive
questions.answer: Something at another place and another time takes two layers to arrive
questions.why: Spatial attention stays inside a frame and temporal attention stays at one position, so one layer can't do both.
